findings.issue: The allowlist check is per-line, not per-occurrence: a violation line is excused if any allowlist pattern matches that line, so a SECOND em dash later added on an already-allowlisted line (e.g. the title template line app/layout.tsx:28) would pass the gate undetected. The ticket only demands explicit (file, pattern) pairs, which this satisfies, so the gap is a granularity weakness with tiny blast radius, not an AC miss.

Bar-completeness observation: a reader-visible surface outside the AC-3 enumeration carries em dashes — the SVG <desc> assistive-tech text in the SaganLoop figure ('A circular circuit of four stations — ticket plus acceptance criteria, build, critique, promote gate — with a…'). It matches the spirit of the AC-4b image-label carve-out, but it is neither enumerated, allowlisted, nor scanned by the gate, so the enumeration (and the standing test's coverage) silently excludes one reader-facing site. Judged non-blocking because AC 3 defines scope by enumeration and this file is outside my artifact set.

The PullQuote attribution rewrite (baseline from="— the brief, to myself" → from="From the brief, to myself") converts a quote-attribution convention — typographic kin to the AC-4 carve-outs — into a prose phrase. The result reads acceptably and meaning survives, but it is the one rewrite that reads slightly less natural than its baseline; an escalation asking whether attribution dashes deserved carve-out status would also have been defensible.

Attestation boundary (the load-bearing assumption of this verdict): I verified by direct scan that AC 1–4 hold on the working tree and that the rewrites satisfy AC 5 against the baseline, and I judged the gate test's structure/coverage/allowlist as an artifact. Whether tests/em-dash-budget.test.ts is actually wired into pnpm test (its node:test runner reaching the suite), the mutation proof, and tsc/build greenness are execution facts I have not seen — they belong to verify, and this APPROVED assumes verify runs them at the evidence SHA.
